messages:
customer-ops: Customer reporting repeated partial SSE payloads then immediate disconnects. They say the client reconnects every ~2s and billing shows tokens for each reconnect. Can we investigate?

alex: Can you paste an example of the raw client behavior and a sample curl repro? Also screenshot of the billing spike would help.

customer-ops: Repro steps from customer: they use a browser client that keeps the connection open but reads slowly. When the response is large they see lines like `data: {...}\n\n` then connection drops. Their minimal curl repro: 

```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=small-ctx" > /dev/null
```

If they throttle the reading side the server eventually closes and the client reconnects. They observe duplicate token counts per reconnect.

lina: Got it. Any server logs from their request?

customer-ops: They provided an excerpt (sanitized):

```
[2024-06-15T14:12:40Z] WARN sse: write error: writev: EAGAIN (Resource temporarily unavailable); buffered_bytes=98304; client_read_rate=12KB/s
[2024-06-15T14:12:40Z] INFO sse: aborting stream: slow consumer threshold exceeded (id=ch_01F...), sent=1200 tokens
[2024-06-15T14:12:42Z] INFO auth: token refresh ok
[2024-06-15T14:12:43Z] INFO sse: new connection from same client (id=ch_01F...), incoming_reconnect=1
```

jess: That looks like the slow consumer path. Runtime aborts after the socket send buffer hits the configured limit and repeated EAGAINs. Reconnects then replay the session creating multiple billed streams.

alex: Can reproduce locally with netcat throttling. Quick repro I used:

```
# server-side: run a simple stream that sends a lot of events
python -m http.server 8000 &
# client: simulate very slow reader
mkfifo /tmp/f; curl -N "http://localhost:8000/large-stream" > /tmp/f &
pv -qL 8 /tmp/f > /dev/null   # limit read to 8 bytes/sec
```

When the server write buffer reaches the threshold we see `EAGAIN` and our stream abort logic kicks in.

sre-bot: FYI: configured default streaming.send_buffer_limit = 96KB; slow_consumer_abort_ms = 30000ms.

lina: For this customer their network RTT is ~400ms and they read slowly; 96KB fills quickly. Short-term mitigations:
- Ask client to implement exponential backoff on reconnects (e.g., 1s -> 2s -> 4s) to avoid reconnect storms.
- Use Last-Event-ID to resume where possible, or have client request incremental deltas instead of full replays.
- Reduce payload size per event (chunking) so the consumer can process smaller units.

jess: Runtime options we can tune for an account (internal):
- increase streaming.send_buffer_limit to 192KB for this customer temporarily (cost: more memory per connection),
- raise slow_consumer_abort_ms to 60s to tolerate slower readers (risk: more buffered data, higher memory & billing duplication if retries happen),
- enable prefix/KV caching on model to make reconnects cheaper.

alex: Billing note: current behavior bills tokens for each completed stream segment. If client reconnects and causes server to re-send the same content, tokens are counted multiple times. We should file a billing follow-up to consider dedup semantics for short reconnects (ticket created: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INFR-4891).

customer-ops: Customer is pushing back because their mobile SDK has unreliable background reads. They want a band-aid while they fix the SDK.

lina: Proposed immediate steps:
1) Offer to increase their account's send_buffer_limit to 192KB for 48 hours and raise slow_consumer_abort_ms to 45s.
2) Provide client-side guidance (exponential backoff, Last-Event-ID, chunking).
3) Escalate runtime to look at adding a metric that tracks duplicate-token-charges per connection.

eng-runtime-oncall: I'm taking this. Can you DM me the account id and an example connection_id? I'll enable a temporary larger buffer and watch memory pressure. Also will add a debug flag to log the sequence of partial frames.

jess: Also note: depending on their network, forcing TCP_NODELAY off or on might change write behavior. Recommend they test toggling Nagle's algorithm in their SDK.

customer-ops: Account id DM'd. They also shared a raw HAR where the client closes the read side then immediately re-opens.

eng-runtime-oncall: Started change: set streaming.send_buffer_limit=196608 for account acct_0123 (applied). Monitoring now for new aborts.

sre-bot: Change applied by eng-runtime-oncall at 2024-06-15T15:01:02Z.

lina: I'll prepare a short KB for customer: how to detect slow reader vs network flakiness, and recommended client-side changes. Draft will include the curl/netcat repro snippet and the server log lines to look for.

alex: Follow-ups: eng-runtime to confirm whether we can make reconnect-resume cheaper (dedupe tokens) and billing to review INFR-4891. Support to update customer with temporary config change and KB.

customer-ops: Thanks everyone. Customer is on standby for the config bump. :pray:
